blocks.text: Japan’s Immigration Services Agency on Wednesday said the former leader of a South Korean opposition party, known for visiting disputed islets in the Sea of Japan, was denied entry into the country due to a criminal conviction. Cho Kuk, a former head of the left-leaning minor opposition Rebuilding Korea Party and a former justice minister, was found guilty of falsifying documents regarding his children’s school admissions. A two-year prison sentence became final in December 2024 before he was pardoned in August last year.
